correctness.rationale: From the twelve explicit rhombic facets, all 14 vertices/24 edges and edge lengths are reconstructed. Seven rational spherical triangles certify every vertex-height comparison and hence the exact three-zone offset interval table. Oriented spherical first-moment integrals over the three triangles reduce the coefficients to the seven displayed arctangent expressions, and the polyhedral mean-width identity fixes the Crofton denominator. The independent edge integral proves the exact expectation six. The delivered checker passes the rational chamber enumeration, closed-form evaluations, normalization, and width-weighted random simulation; numerical samples are not the proof.

The checked same-body Socha paper does not provide that joint distribution.

originality.rationale: The exact per-plane seven-atom count law was not found in verified primary same-object references or semantic literature and mathematical-record searches. Socha 1988 studies pooled section-angle statistics, not the random polygon side-count distribution; Koca et al. 2014 give the object construction, not its Crofton section law. Earlier independent distributions for boxes and cuboctahedra cannot imply the exact rhombic-dodecahedral probabilities. Historic priority remains qualified by identified inaccessible older literature.
residual_risks: H. Adrian (1986), a Polish conference contribution on plane-angle distributions, was cited in Socha 1988 but not independently obtainable in full; historical tables from that simulation could exist, though exact seven-atom formulas are not established by the accessible descriptions.
Some pre-digital stereology literature and archival tables might contain section-side frequencies or exact evaluations not indexed by the searches.
The publisher-hosted full text of Melmore (1942) was not accessible; only its abstract was read, so no conclusive whole-paper exclusion is asserted.
No independent historical-priority review has been performed.

value.rationale: The seven exact probabilities classify all generic polygon types of a canonical space-filling Catalan solid under a natural invariant stereological experiment, including a nontrivial exact quadrilateral probability, the exact mean and an especially small nonagonal atom. The three-chamber normal structure and seven surviving offset classes have geometric content; this is not just a scalar numerical exercise, a previously published table, or a reparameterization of another solid.
